title: Chromosomal Disorders
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: Chromosomal Disorders
Standard clinical genetics teaching; ACOG aneuploidy screening

changelog.change: Initial entry — trisomies 21/13/18 with associated anomalies and recurrence risk, and the sex-chromosome aneuploidies.

purpose: Recognise the common aneuploidies from the newborn exam, know the associated anomalies to screen for, and give families accurate recurrence-risk information (which depends on the mechanism — free trisomy vs a translocation).

items: Mechanism: nondisjunction / free trisomy 21 (~ 95%), Robertsonian translocation (~ 3–4%), mosaicism (~ 1–2%).

Exam: flat facial profile, upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthal folds, Brushfield spots, small ears, single transverse palmar crease, 5th-finger clinodactyly, a wide 1st–2nd toe gap; hypotonia, hyperextensible joints, weak Moro.

Screen for: congenital heart disease (~ 40–50%, especially AV septal defect — echo every infant), duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung disease, congenital hypothyroidism (and lifelong thyroid surveillance), transient myeloproliferative disorder / increased leukaemia risk, atlantoaxial instability, hearing loss, cataracts.
Recurrence: free trisomy 21 → ~ 1% above the maternal-age baseline. Translocation → obtain PARENTAL karyotypes; a balanced-carrier parent has a substantially higher, translocation-specific risk.

rows: Cleft lip/palate, microphthalmia, holoprosencephaly spectrum, postaxial polydactyly, cutis aplasia (scalp defects), CHD
Growth restriction, prominent occiput, micrognathia, clenched hands with overlapping fingers, rocker-bottom feet, CHD (VSD common)
Most die within the first year
Most die within the first year

body.text: Confirm with a karyotype. Management is individualised with the family — a growing number of centres offer selective interventions rather than uniformly comfort-only care.

rows: Short stature, webbed neck, low posterior hairline, broad chest / widely spaced nipples, coarctation of the aorta, bicuspid aortic valve, horseshoe kidney, ovarian dysgenesis → infertility, lymphoedema of the hands/feet in the newborn
Tall stature, small firm testes, infertility, gynaecomastia, learning difficulties — often diagnosed late
The commonest inherited cause of intellectual disability; long narrow face, large ears, macro-orchidism after puberty, autism features
Tall stature, usually normal IQ, a mild increase in learning/behavioural difficulty in some

body.text: Prenatal aneuploidy screening: nuchal translucency, first-trimester combined (PAPP-A, free β-hCG), quad screen, and cell-free DNA. All are SCREENS — a positive result is confirmed with a diagnostic karyotype/microarray on CVS or amniocentesis.

buildNote: Newborn recognition + associated-anomaly screening + recurrence-risk counselling.
